statements.status_notes: Upstream GCC commit 5d419c69ce2e6b86d7da75f18736904885674219 (PR libstdc++/124370) stops std::bitset wide-character stream extraction from sizing its buffer without sizeof(wchar_t). The fix is backported to Debian's gcc-14 14.2.0-19 source for trixie, re-expressed against the 14.2.0 operator>>. Debian trixie has not published the fix; see https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-115455

Upstream GCC commit 2fd8866591b5aea7098835f80ab7e176382175ae makes std::vector<bool> constructors check the element count against max_size() before sizing the bit array, so the word count cannot wrap. The fix is backported to Debian's gcc-14 14.2.0-19 source for trixie, without the from_range constructor hunk, which GCC 14.2.0 does not have. Debian trixie has not published the fix; see https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-114691

Upstream GCC commit c1f32b67510f6f9998deadaef5090b6663adb979 sizes the parallel std::search border table one element larger so the border computation cannot index past it. The fix is backported to Debian's gcc-14 14.2.0-19 source for trixie. Debian trixie has not published the fix; see https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-114690

GO-2026-5932 is scoped exclusively to the deprecated golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp package tree (and subpackages), which is frozen upstream with no fixed module release. Scout matches golang.org/x/crypto at the module level because the advisory records the module with no fixed version. The golang-msft-fips toolchain is built from microsoft/go; repository code search shows no import of golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp under src/cmd or elsewhere in src. go.mod lists golang.org/x/crypto as a bootstrap module dependency, but the openpgp subpackage is not compiled into the shipped go/compiler binaries (vulnerable_code_not_present).

GO-2026-5932 is scoped exclusively to the deprecated golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp package tree (and subpackages), which is frozen upstream with no fixed module release. Scout matches golang.org/x/crypto at the module level because the advisory records the module with no fixed version. The dhi-kserve APK ships manager, agent, router, localmodel, and localmodelnode binaries built from kserve v0.20; none of these binaries import or link golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp, so the vulnerable OpenPGP code is not present in the shipped artifacts (vulnerable_code_not_present).

GO-2026-5932 is scoped exclusively to the deprecated golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp package tree, which is frozen upstream with no fixed module release; see https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5932. The docker-engine APK ships dockerd built from Moby 29.7.2, which vendors github.com/ProtonMail/go-crypto for OpenPGP and does not import golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp. go version -m on the published dockerd binary lists golang.org/x/crypto v0.55.0 as a module dependency but no golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp import path, so the advisory OpenPGP code is not present in the shipped artifact.
